symptom: After an exec that wrote, `select … from CATALOG.ACTIVITIES` (or refs, widgets, the graph views) answered 0 / partial rows, with only a progress-line 'requires refresh catalog full' warning; within one session it answered from the stale in-memory catalog instead.
cause: execCatalogQuery always asked ensureCatalog for fast mode and only when no catalog was in memory: a write changes the .mpr, the cache is then invalid, and the rebuild was a fast in-memory catalog that fills none of the full-mode tables.
fix: requiredCatalogMode(tables) picks fast/full/source from the tables the query names; catalogCurrent checks the session catalog's mode, .mpr and mod time; ensureCatalogMode rebuilds at that mode through the existing incremental, never-narrow path and saves the cache.
insight: Measured on TestApp (900 unit files): cold full build 3.6 s; one created microflow then a CATALOG.ACTIVITIES query 0.37 s ('incremental: 1 units rebuilt, 703 carried over'). A warning an agent must read and act on costs a round trip and tokens; when the fix is a sub-second incremental build, do it instead of warning. The in-session case only surfaces with a test that keeps the catalog in memory, the new-process case only with one that drops it — test both.
test: mdl/executor/catalog_query_rebuilds_2200_test.go TestCatalogQuery_RebuildsTheModeItsTablesNeed (fails on the old path with 0 activities in a new session and a stale cache)
